summary: Registers media types for the Ogg container format and sets conformance requirements for implementations of them. It covers the general Ogg type along with variants for audio and video. It replaces RFC 3534, and has been updated by a later document.

eli5.summary: A file label tells your computer what is inside. This gives the Ogg multimedia file format official labels, so browsers and players know how to open it.

what file extension does ogg use
subtitle: Registers application/ogg, video/ogg and audio/ogg so Ogg files can be labelled correctly on the wire.

tldr.problem: Ogg content was labelled with application/ogg in an ad hoc way, which hides whether the data is audio or video and left some aspects underspecified.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC redefines application/ogg for complex multiplexed data, registers video/ogg and audio/ogg, adds file extensions and an optional codecs parameter, and recommends the Ogg Skeleton bitstream.
tldr.outcome: Ogg content can be identified more precisely. The RFC obsoletes RFC 3534 and has been updated by RFC 7845.

today: RFC 5334 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 3534 and has been updated by RFC 7845. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Introduction and Changes
sections.content:
Ogg is a data encapsulation format defined by the Xiph.Org Foundation. Binary data in Ogg, such as Vorbis and Theora, had historically been exchanged using application/ogg as defined by RFC 3534. This document obsoletes that RFC and defines three media types for different kinds of Ogg content.

The media types are needed to identify Ogg content when it is served over HTTP, included in multi-part documents or used elsewhere that media types are used. Ogg itself suits stream-based storage such as files and transport such as TCP streams or pipes.

Compared with RFC 3534, application/ogg is redefined, video/ogg and audio/ogg are defined, new file extensions and Macintosh file type codes are defined, an optional codecs parameter is defined, and Ogg Skeleton becomes a recommended addition.
sections.eli5: Ogg is a kind of box for audio and video. This RFC gives the box proper labels so players know what to expect.

sections.title: Three Types and How They Relate
sections.content:
Using the application top-level type for audio and video is problematic because it obscures what the content is. So video/ogg and audio/ogg SHOULD be used for video and audio content respectively.

application/ogg now covers complex data, such as multitrack visual, audio, textual and other time-continuously sampled data that is not clearly audio or video. It is the recommended choice for scientific and other applications needing multiplexed signals or streams, with or without scriptable control. It embraces the widest range of content, with video/ogg and audio/ogg as smaller subsets.

video/ogg is recommended for visual or timed-text material that is not complex enough to need application/ogg. audio/ogg is an even smaller subset, recommended when the bitstream predominantly contains audio (lyrics, metadata or cover art notwithstanding).
sections.eli5: There is a big bin for anything complicated, a smaller bin for video, and a smallest bin for music. Put each file in the smallest bin it fits.

sections.title: Skeleton and the Codecs Parameter
sections.content:
An Ogg bitstream consists of one or more logical bitstreams. An Ogg Skeleton bitstream lets software identify their content types without decoding their header pages. Skeleton is REQUIRED for application/ogg and RECOMMENDED for video/ogg and audio/ogg.

An implementation that finds a logical bitstream it cannot decode SHOULD ignore it and keep decoding the others, which keeps it compatible with existing and future data.

The types can optionally carry the codecs parameter from RFC 4281. The RFC maps the identifier at the start of the first header page of each codec to a string, for example theora, vorbis, speex, flac, dirac and cmml. Examples are video/ogg; codecs="theora, vorbis" and audio/ogg; codecs=speex.
sections.eli5: Skeleton is like a table of contents inside the file. The codecs label says which kinds of audio or video are packed in.

sections.title: The Registrations
sections.content:
The IANA section registers two new media types and redefines the existing application/ogg. All three have the first four bytes 0x4f 0x67 0x67 0x53, the string OggS, as their magic number, cite RFC 3533 as the published specification, and name the Xiph.Org Foundation as change controller.

The file extensions differ. application/ogg uses .ogx, replacing the .ogg extension of RFC 3534 because some implementations expect .ogg to be Vorbis-only audio. video/ogg uses .ogv. audio/ogg uses .oga, .ogg and .spx; the last two mean Vorbis-only and Speex-only files and need no Skeleton for backward compatibility.
sections.eli5: Each bin gets its own file ending, like .ogv for video and .oga for audio, so you can tell them apart by name.

sections.title: Security and Encoding
sections.content:
Ogg content is binary, an unrestricted sequence of octets. It should be transmitted without CR/LF conversion or 7-bit stripping, and base64 is generally preferred for binary-to-text encoding.

Ogg is only a container and is not more vulnerable than other content framing. It has no generic encryption or signing, though it can carry encrypted or signed content. Because it can hold any binary data, executable content is possible, and implementations SHOULD NOT execute it without the end-user validating its origin. Decoders must handle manipulated bitstreams and buffer overflows, and SHOULD protect themselves against malicious streams that ask for an excessively large picture size or high sampling-rate audio.
sections.eli5: The box itself is harmless, but what is inside might not be. Do not run surprise programs from it, and be careful with files that claim to be gigantic.
